description: The image consists of three side-by-side grouped vertical bar charts, labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4, which illustrate Perplexity across different Quantization Bits for two distinct methods. In all three charts, the horizontal axis represents the categories, labeled "Quantization Bits," with discrete values ordered numerically as 3, 4, 8, and 16. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "Perplexity," using a linear scale. For charts (a) and (c), the vertical axis ranges from 0 to slightly above 30, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5. For chart (b), the vertical axis ranges from 0 to slightly above 400, with tick marks at regular intervals of 50. The bars are grouped by Quantization Bits, with each group containing two side-by-side bars. According to the legends, the blue bars represent the "Uniform" method (though the text is partially obscured in chart a), and the orange bars represent the "Ours" method. All bars feature a solid black outline. Across all three charts, the blue "Uniform" bars are consistently taller than the orange "Ours" bars within each group, and values generally decrease as quantization bits increase from 3 to 4, before leveling off. In chart (a) WikiText, the highest value is the Uniform bar at 3 bits (approximately 31), and the lowest is the Ours bar at 8 and 16 bits (approximately 18.5). In chart (b) PTB, the tallest bar is Uniform at 3 bits (approximately 420), while the shortest is Ours at 4 bits (approximately 178). In chart (c) C4, the maximum value is Uniform at 3 bits (approximately 30), and the minimum is Ours at 8 and 16 bits (approximately 17.5). The categories on the horizontal axis are sorted in ascending numerical order, and there are no additional visual emphases such as shading or annotations.
